chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Dave Kapp at Decca: blues and folk repertoire, then Frenesi
summary: Dave Kapp gave him a free hand with folk and blues records like the Blues on Parade series, yet also pushed him to sing Frenesi.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, yeah, to some degree I think I did. I'm pretty sure I did, because -- and when I didn't, I was being shoved and pushed around by the powers that be at Decca, because they really knew what they wanted, and I learned a great deal from their operation, Jack and particularly Dave Kapp. Because Dave was the guy that used to take the truck out, the sound truck, and go into the South and try to discover folk and blues and people, and do it right on the spot. And he had a goodly supply and an unlimited kind of repertoire to offer things for me to record.
Which led to such things as "Troubling Mind, Dupree Blues," and so on and so on and so on. And he made me more and more aware of a certain kind of American folk and blues kind of thing.
He was a big influence in his day.
-- that -- I think it was eight or ten 78's, records in the Blues on Parade album. That was kind of a --

And he gave me a pretty free hand on any of those things. Once he got the idea to make -- but by the same token, he would turn around and in the same week that he gave me two or three of these things, would turn around and call me in and say, this record is breaking very big over on RCA Victor, but I've got a lyric written for you and I want you to sing. I'll give you the title in just a second. (Singing.)
Frennessee, right. So where Hardy had a big record on this instrumentally, we did very well. We sold a lot of records with my singing way up in the air with a lot of muted trumpets in the background.
So they were very helpful in a lot of ways, and it was always -- they knew what they were seeking, and I was still finding where I wanted to go. So a lot of
times, I think I did, and so did the guys in the band, feel we were being maneuvered. But it was probably best for us in the long run.
